content.text: {"headline":"Approve P3: full response with the remaining overtime budget. It is the only option that reaches the 80% target (81.4%) for 15:15-17:15, at ₹1,902 extra.","why":"The surge is caused by the UPI outage (P1 incident INC-20261027-4076), not by staffing. 'UPI payment failed' calls are running at 2.24x normal, and absences and handle time are normal. So the fix needs both lower outage demand and more payments capacity. P3 combines an IVR outage message, 20% chat deflection, overtime for 7 payments agents (15:45-16:45), cancelled payments coaching, 8 cross-skilled agents moved from general (16:00-17:00), delayed breaks and IVR callback. It is predicted to lift service level to 81.4% overall (payments 77.8%, general 90.0%) and cut abandons to 3.2%, versus 57.0% and 10.5% with no action. Rest-of-day service level improves to 86.6%. There are no policy violations and no escalation is needed.","trade_offs":["P2 (outage message, deflection, agent move, delayed breaks) costs ₹792, ₹1,110 less than P3, but reaches only 75.8% (payments 69.8%) with 5.0% abandons. It falls short of target.","P1 (no-cost shuffle, ₹450) does no better than doing nothing: 56.8% vs 57.0%, with payments at 44.9%. Moving agents alone doesn't touch the outage demand.","Risk to general is low. General holds at 90.0% under P3 despite losing 8 agents for 16:00-17:00.","P3 uses the remaining overtime budget, leaving no overtime headroom if the outage runs past 17:15."],"watch":"Payments service level and abandons from 15:45, when overtime starts, and again at 16:00, when the agent move and callback begin. Also watch the status of INC-20261027-4076. If UPI isn't restored by about 17:00, or payments stays well below 77.8%, involve the duty manager, because there is no overtime budget left."}
